lens: CHEAT DETECTOR, round 2 verification (hardcoding, oracle, weld, teleport, scope, planner invariance). Answers to the special questions: D4 is a declared extra sensor, not a ground-truth oracle, and is acceptable as the thesis's fixed-eye model only with N5 (robot self-occlusion) and N10 (headline wording). D5/M1 is a planned move the planner must achieve through move + plan-motion, not the archived park, but only if N2 (motion-layer ledger) and N3 (planner identity) hold, and its adoption rule reads the test layouts (N8). D6 uses no ground truth and no per-object flag, but its observational premise is never checked (C8) and is false behind the robot's hand (N5). D7's home_not_reached is a termination bound, not a scripted choice, but it can never fire as specified (N4). tampura_policy_timed as worded requires overriding TAMPURA's rollout or patching their env (N6). Archive check: G5 catches boxel_policy.py:253-258 (all_shadows as known_empty, no render provenance) and G4 catches _next_place_xy (:160-176); G3 does NOT catch the parks at :295-296 and :346-347 (execute_go_home called outside any dispatcher, so the dispatcher-emitted ledger never sees them, N2); G11 does NOT catch the archived planner subclass with a swapped domain (planner_boxel.py:28-49) while G10 is conditional (N3); G14 does not cover the executing arm (N2); G20 needs a module-level render hook (N2).

unresolved_round1.why_unresolved: The revision adopts the rule (an interior region is never cast at a place destination) but not the check C8 required: 'G5 admits this provenance class explicitly and the gate asserts the free-cell observation precedes the placement'. Nothing verifies the premise per placement. The rule is keyed to the code path (registration vs place), not to the observation record, so a relocated hollow body that the integrity monitor retires and a later render re-registers (world_integrity_check lost/retire, execution.py:1832-1878; register_new_detections, execution.py:2255; shadow recast on rediscovery, execution.py:2948-3003) gets an unknown interior at a destination the robot chose, re-opening the respawn loop that C8 described, bounded only by F9's three strikes (execution.py:2960-2971). The premise is also false behind the robot's hand (N5).
unresolved_round1.required_change: At every place, log the cavity footprint at the destination and assert it lies within cells whose not-here status carries render provenance or within SHADOW fragments still registered in the belief. At any registration of a hollow body the same test decides: interior status unknown if the footprint contains space without that provenance, otherwise not_here with provenance 'observed before placement' written to the ledger, which G5 admits as an explicit class. The observation record decides in every case, never the code path.

new_findings.title: Gravity and our own robot set-up are unspecified on the adopt-client path; find_dice never sets gravity, so our 'physical' execution can silently run in zero g
new_findings.problem: B3(b) adopts their client with 'no resetSimulation, no _setup_scene'. BoxelTestEnv sets gravity only beside resetSimulation (boxel_env.py:510-511) and applies its grasp preconditions inside _setup_scene: finger-pad lateral friction 1.2 (boxel_env.py:810-812) and fingers opened to 0.04 (boxel_env.py:824-828). TAMPURA's find_dice never calls setGravity (grep over tampura_environments hits only class_uncertain/env.py:334, tool_use/env.py:308, puck_slide/env.py:258; setup_robot_pybullet, panda_env_utils.py:844-851, and the tampura package have none), so their executing client has PyBullet's default zero gravity. Unless someone adds it, grasps cannot slip, placed cups cannot fall, the 1 cm float persists, and B1(c)/D9's settle displacement reads 0 and certifies nothing: a global weld equivalent. The plan never mentions gravity (no hit for 'gravity' in plan_v2.txt), and D9's 'Nothing else of theirs is altered' read literally forbids setting it. The pad friction and finger opening are neither applied nor rejected, so they will be decided at B7 after grasps slip, an outcome-driven change. G14's trap list has no setGravity, setPhysicsEngineParameter or setTimeStep.
new_findings.evidence: boxel_env.py:510-511, 810-812, 824-828; scratchpad tampura_environments_full grep 'gravity' (find_dice absent); panda_env_utils.py:844-851; plan D9 lines 417-427, B3(b) lines 531-533, G14 lines 158-165
new_findings.required_change: D9 pre-registers the complete physics configuration written into their executing client before the first step: setGravity(0, 0, -9.81) cited to boxel_env.py:511; the pad friction decision made now with its reason (our 1.2 from boxel_env.py:810-812 as 'our gripper', or their URDF value); the initial finger opening. Each is a G1/G14 allowlist entry with a BF#. B1(c) asserts gravity == -9.81 via getPhysicsEngineParameters before measuring the settle; campaign.json records gravity, timestep and friction values; G14 also traps setGravity, setPhysicsEngineParameter, setTimeStep and changeDynamics on the robot after the first step; the paper states that TAMPURA's arm runs without gravity and ours with it.

new_findings.title: Runtime gates cannot see out-of-band robot motion or state writes: the archived parks pass G3, an arm teleport home passes G14, and trap exceptions can be swallowed
new_findings.plan_location: G3, G5, G8(b), G14, G20, B0 (ledger in the dispatcher)
new_findings.problem: B0 puts the ledger 'in the main dispatcher', so a primitive executed outside the dispatcher (from execute_fn before or after main(), or from the env adapter) emits no record and G3's 'zero executed primitives without a (plan id, step index)' is vacuously true. The archived parks were exactly that: execute_go_home called from the policy, outside any dispatcher (archive boxel_policy.py:295-296, 346-347); the same park through robot_utils.move_robot_smooth passes G1 (not a forbidden call), G14 (not a teleport) and G3. G14 traps only 'task bodies', so a resetJointState of the executing ARM to DEFAULT_ARM_POS before scoring makes D3's joint readback pass their 1e-4 test: the CB#123 cheat moved from the belief into the simulator. G5 checks only ids passed as known_empty, but a fragment removed from the registry (sweep_all_fragments does registry.remove_boxel after classifying, execution.py:2236-2237) leaves the planner's init without passing through known_empty, so an unobserved removal is invisible. G8(b)/G14 traps 'raise', but main-pipeline readers swallow broad exceptions (world_eye.py:172-176, telemetry.py:201-205: except Exception: continue). G20 is 'checked and logged per render' with no stated hook; the archived segment_visible rendered through client.getCameraImage with its own 60 degree projection (archive perception_adapter.py:110-115), bypassing any detect_objects-level check.
new_findings.evidence: plan B0 lines 453-455, G3 lines 85-92, G14 lines 158-165; archive boxel_policy.py:295-296, 346-347; test_full_pipeline.py:1583 (the only move_robot_smooth call in main(), inside the dispatcher); execution.py:2236-2237; world_eye.py:172-176; telemetry.py:201-205; archive perception_adapter.py:110-115
new_findings.required_change: (a) Motion-layer hook on the executing client: pybullet.setJointMotorControl2/Array and robot_utils.move_robot_smooth on the robot's arm and finger joints assert an active dispatcher context (plan id, step index) set and cleared by the dispatcher; any command outside it fails G3. (b) G14 covers the executing robot body (all joints) as well as task bodies; only the pre-registered set-up writes before the first step are allowed. (c) The scoring adapter logs the arm readback at main() return and at observation build; a difference beyond settle noise fails G6. (d) G5 covers every SHADOW boxel (lateral or interior) that leaves the registry or changes status, each needing a classifier record (render id, outcome) written at the classifier call site. (e) Every runtime trap increments a violation counter read after the episode (fail on any count > 0) besides raising. (f) G20 is a module-level pybullet.getCameraImage hook on every client; write-only captures are declared by name.

new_findings.title: Planner identity is ungated when M1 is dropped: the archived planner subclass with a swapped domain passes G11, and M1 has no declared domain switch
new_findings.problem: The archived planner was BoxelBridgePlanner(PDDLStreamPlanner), which skipped __init__, set self.domain_pddl to domain_find_dice_streamful.pddl and self.streams to the bridge streams, and inherited plan() (archive planner_boxel.py:28-49). G11(i) passes (it imports pddlstream_planner, not pddlstream), G11(ii) passes (solve's caller frame is the inherited PDDLStreamPlanner.plan), G11(iii) passes. G10, the only domain check, applies 'only if M1 is adopted'. M1 itself needs a domain switch B3 does not provide: PDDLStreamPlanner.__init__ hardcodes read_pddl_file('domain_pddlstream.pddl') (pddlstream_planner.py:177), main() builds the planner itself (test_full_pipeline.py:952), and B3(c)'s three keyword arguments include no domain parameter, so B4 would be wired by an unreviewed injection, the archived pattern.
new_findings.evidence: archive planner_boxel.py:28-49; pddlstream_planner.py:33, 177-178, 1131; test_full_pipeline.py:952; plan G10 lines 134-138, G11 lines 139-146, B3(c) lines 534-540
new_findings.required_change: G10 runs unconditionally: at every plan() call, sha256 of planner.domain_pddl and planner.stream_pddl equals pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl and pddl/stream.pddl (or the regenerated M1 file); type(planner) is PDDLStreamPlanner and type(planner.streams) is streams.BoxelStreams exactly, no subclass. B3(c) adds an explicit domain-file keyword (default today's file, byte-identical) so M1 selects its generated domain through a declared argument; the solve hook wraps the name bound in pddlstream_planner (it imports solve at module load, :33).

new_findings.title: D7's home_not_reached bound can never fire, and D7 needs B4's init delta even when M1 is dropped
new_findings.problem: After a move the loop sets current_config = RobotConfig(readback, name=q2.name) (test_full_pipeline.py:1591-1597), and RobotConfig equality and hash are by name (streams.py:118-124). After a move home that misses 1e-4, the next init asserts at_config(q_home), the goal holds symbolically, plan() returns [] (pddlstream_planner.py:1202-1209), the dispatcher runs nothing, the D7-extended _loop_done stays false, and the loop replans until the 900 s cap. No second move is ever planned, so 'two consecutive moves to q_home that leave the evaluator false' never happens; the episode is censored with a wrong exit reason, and the improvised fix will be an unplanned re-home servo, the CB#120(g) pattern. Separately, move requires (config_for_boxel ?q2 ?b) (domain_pddlstream.pddl:215) and only compute-kin and compute-stack-kin certify it (stream.pddl:28, 39), so the goal at_config(q_home) has no grounded move unless _build_init emits B4's (Boxel home)(config_for_boxel q_home home), which the plan schedules only if M1 is adopted. The final-hold 'A/B on our scenes' is vacuous because our scenes declare no goal configuration.
new_findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:1591-1597, 1201-1209; streams.py:118-124; pddlstream_planner.py:1202-1209; pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl:207-223; pddl/stream.pddl:24-39; plan D7 lines 384-399, B4 lines 556-567
new_findings.required_change: Pre-register in D7: when the at_config evaluator fails after a move to a declared goal configuration, current_config is renamed from the readback (q_readback_k) so the planner's init is honest and the planner itself plans the corrective move; home_not_reached then counts planned moves. This is a B3 main-loop change with its own BF#. Move B4's home pseudo-boxel init facts and their type-check assertions under D7, unconditional for the bridge and covered by G10; only the sense precondition stays conditional on B1(h). Label the final hold a bridge-only executor mode whose A/B on our scenes shows only that it is inert.

new_findings.title: 'Free space is observed space' is false behind the robot's own hand in the D4 eye; those cells get Know-If not-here without any observation
new_findings.problem: The plan says the hand is in frame when the arm is at home (D4: 'When the arm is at home its hand is in frame exactly as in their check'), and the first render is taken there. The robot is excluded from detections (boxel_env.py:1751) and casts no shadow (shadow_calculator.py has no robot handling), so the table area hidden behind the hand becomes octree free space, and with observed_clear_regions None the planner emits obj_at_boxel_KIF for the target on every free boxel (pddlstream_planner.py:604-612, 679-681) on the stated assumption that the camera sees the whole table. D8 intersects the window with the frustum but not with the robot's occlusion, and D6 rests its no-interior-at-destination rule on that premise. This is a belief update without observation, the class of the archived all_shadows write, at model level; on these 20 seeds it is harmless only because the die is always under a cup, which is task knowledge, not a justification.
new_findings.evidence: plan D4 lines 329-331, D6 lines 370-373, D8 lines 412-414; boxel_env.py:1751; pddlstream_planner.py:604-612, 667-681; shadow_calculator.py (no 'robot' match)
new_findings.required_change: B1(e) measures, in the D4 eye's render at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, the table-plane footprint covered by the robot's seg id; D8's workspace window subtracts it (or the robot at home casts a SHADOW region like any occluder, an explicit model tweak with its own BF#); D6's justification and the paper cite the subtraction and state the removed area.

new_findings.title: tampura_policy_timed cannot wrap env.step without overriding TAMPURA's rollout or patching their env: an edit of arm T's measured loop in disguise
new_findings.problem: env.step is called inside Policy.rollout (tampura/policies/policy.py:129), which also owns the clock (st at :104, time_deltas via history.add at :136 and :153). A Policy subclass can time env.step only by overriding rollout (copying their loop into our code, where any drift in step count, early stop or clock placement changes arm T's numbers) or by assigning a wrapper to the env instance's step attribute (an instance patch that G13's 'no monkeypatch of their classes' does not cover). Either way arm T no longer runs TAMPURA's loop as shipped.
new_findings.evidence: <git>/tampura/tampura/policies/policy.py:96-159; tampura/environment.py:49-65; plan P4.6 lines 740-746, G13 lines 155-157
new_findings.required_change: tampura_policy_timed overrides get_action only (super().get_action inside perf_counter, the span written into info or a side log) and inherits rollout; per-step env.step plus update time is derived as the time_deltas increment minus the get_action span. G13 asserts type(policy).rollout is Policy.rollout, the subclass __dict__ holds only __init__ and get_action, and the env has no instance attribute 'step'. B1(g)'s as-shipped block must reproduce arm T's per-seed outcomes under the same seeds; any difference is reported.

new_findings.title: The fallback lets an unfavourable B7 outcome remove the same-environment numbers from the paper
new_findings.plan_location: P4.4 CALENDAR / FALLBACK, B7, M5 RULE
new_findings.problem: 'FALLBACK if B7 is not clean by 2026-11-20: ... reports no bridge numbers.' 'Clean' is undefined, and B7 is two watched episodes whose outcomes are seen before the go/no-go. If our arm fails them on the merits, the fallback publishes the indirect comparison and omits the same-environment result, contradicting M5's own rule ('a worse result is written as such') and the user's 'see who did better'.
new_findings.evidence: plan lines 596-598 (B7 abort and GO/NO-GO), 616-620 (FALLBACK), 690-691 (M5 RULE)
new_findings.required_change: Define the B7 GO criterion on infrastructure only: every gate green, ledger complete, no crash, G6 controls pass; episode success is explicitly not a criterion. On NO-GO the paper states that the same-environment comparison was attempted and why it stopped, reports B7's per-episode outcomes, and does not present the indirect comparison as evidence of parity.

new_findings.title: Two pre-registered decision rules read the test instances
new_findings.problem: B1(h) decides M1 by rendering 'each cup's interior region grid', i.e. the cups of the three released layouts, whose poses come from problems/*.json, a source G9 forbids. D11 checks only 'the d and e class widths', the classes singled out because the die hides under them in every layout (P4.2), so the hidden object's location selects what the gripper rule checks. Neither hardcodes a solution (YCB cup sizes grow a to e, so the d/e test happens to cover a to c), but both are model decisions fitted to the test set.
new_findings.evidence: plan D5 lines 349-354, D11 lines 435-437, P4.2 lines 208-211, G9 lines 128-133
new_findings.required_change: B1(h) evaluates a scene-independent set: each hollow class's interior footprint at every cell of the D8 window (or M1 is adopted unconditionally). D11 checks every cup class present in the scenes' category table (a..e). Both rules cite only class meshes, the URDF and the window.

new_findings.title: G2, G8(b) and G16 are red by construction against the main pipeline's write-only diagnostics and inherited methods (the C3 pattern again)
new_findings.problem: world_eye reads the true pose and AABB of every env.objects entry, hidden target included, on every snapshot (world_eye.py:166-181; called per plan and per action at test_full_pipeline.py:1353, 1495); telemetry reads every body (telemetry.py:200-208, 267-271, 308-318); execution.py carries print-only ground-truth diagnostics (605-606, 657-658, 1132, 1260); D9 logs each task body's settle displacement from true poses. None is on the G2 or G8(b) exception list ('plan-twin static branch and the scoring adapter'). G16 says main(oracle_phases=False) 'raises if the env exposes oracle_detect_objects at all', but B2's adapter is a BoxelTestEnv subclass and inherits oracle_detect_objects (boxel_env.py:1792), so the check is red unless weakened.
new_findings.required_change: Pre-register a write-only allowlist (world_eye, telemetry, the named execution.py diagnostic lines, a post-episode D9 settle module) with a test that none of their values reaches registry, belief, planner or executor (or disable them on the bridge path with an A/B), and state it in G2 and G8(b). G16 becomes 'call counter == 0, and the adapter overrides oracle_detect_objects and update_object_positions to raise', not an attribute test.

new_findings.title: The M5 headline credits 'our planner' and omits the sensor asymmetry
new_findings.problem: The template reads 'our planner reached the goal in X/20 ... against Y/20 for TAMPURA'. D1 makes arm O the whole pipeline (B9 is the planner-only variant), and D4 gives it a fixed eye that observes after every action, a sensor TAMPURA's robot does not have; the difference appears only in the table notes, so the headline reads as a planner comparison under equal sensing.
new_findings.evidence: plan M5 lines 686-689, D1 lines 284-289, D4 lines 339-340, P4.6 DISCLOSURES lines 785-795
new_findings.required_change: Template: 'our pipeline (a fixed camera at TAMPURA's home wrist-camera pose, observing after every action) reached the goal in X/20 ... against Y/20 for TAMPURA (wrist camera, observing on look)'; the identity map and task-knowledge disclosures stay in the notes.
